title: SCDF’s myResponder Mobile Application
summary: This page explains the SCDF's myResponder Mobile Application, its purpose, and how it can be used to save lives and mitigate minor fires.

title: myResponder Mobile Application
summary: This page explains the myResponder mobile application by SCDF to alert members of the public to nearby fire and medical cases, and save lives.
subtopics: myResponder works by notifying members of the public – also known as Community First Responders (CFRs) – of cardiac arrest and fire cases within 400m of their location.
myResponder will also highlight nearby AEDs that may be available to responders, and provide guided advisories in the mitigation of minor fires.

CFRs can then proceed to the stated location and assist by performing CPR or applying an AED to revive the patient, mitigating minor fires using available extinguishing means, or providing further information to SCDF’s 995 Operations Centre.

title: Respiratory Emergencies
summary: Recognize and respond to respiratory emergencies, including laboured breathing, cyanosis, and cardiac arrest.
subtopics: Find out from the casualty what happened to him to determine the cause for his breathing difficulty, if he is conscious.
Perform the Primary Survey and commence CPR and use the AED if the casualty is not breathing.
If the casualty does not respond, call 995 for SCDF.
Check to see whether there are any obstruction s in the mouth, e.g. foreign bodies, food, dentures, vomitus etc.
If the casualty is unconscious but breathing normally, place him/her in the recovery position (see Chapter 2). However, do not turn or move the casualty if neck or spinal injury is suspected.
Do not leave the casualty unattended at any time. Monitor the casualty and record the vital signs at regular intervals.

title: Recognition
summary: Foreign Body Airway Obstruction (FBAO) can be either partial or complete. Coughing is the body’s natural defence against airway obstruction.

title: Chest Thrusts
summary: Alternative technique for relieving obstruction in obese or pregnant casualties.
subtopics: Ask if the casualty is choking
Wrap arms around the casualty's abdomen
Make a fist with one hand
Place thumb-side of fist on the middle of the casualty's sternum
Grasp fist with other hand and bring yourself close to the casualty
Check the mouth and remove any foreign body
Continue with 30 chest compressions and check the mouth after every 30 chest compressions

title: Chest Compressions
summary: Instructions for performing chest compressions on an unconscious choking casualty.
subtopics: Wrap the arms around the casualty’s abdomen
Place your arms under the casualty’s armpits encircling the chest
Make a fist with one hand with the thumb in the palm
Place thumb-side of fist on the middle of the casualty’s sternum
Grasp your fist with your other hand and bring yourself close to the casualty
Deliver each backward thrust firmly and distinctly
Continue with 30 chest compressions and check the mouth after every 30 chest compressions
Support and position the casualty lying on his/her back on a firm flat surface
Call 995 for SCDF and get an AED if visible and nearby
Locate the landmark and perform 30 chest compressions using the same location and techniques as Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation

summary: Provides instructions on applying a tourniquet to control life-threatening external hemorrhage from limb injury.
subtopics: Use a broad-fold triangular bandage from the First Aid kit

title: Recognition and Actions to Take for Rib Fracture
summary: This page provides information on recognizing the signs and symptoms of a rib fracture, as well as actions to take for treatment.
evidence_keywords: pain on taking deep breaths or coughing
presence of shock in the casualty

title: Actions to Take
summary: Actions to take for various types of fractures, including upper arm, elbow, forearm, and wrist fractures.
subtopics: For a fractured rib: Call 995 for SCDF. Reassure the casualty. Place soft padding between the injured side of the chest and arm. Support the limb on the injured side in an elevated arm sling. Tie a broad-fold bandage across the chest.

For open (puncture) chest wound or multiple rib fractures: Call 995 for SCDF. Leave the entry wound open and apply direct pressure over the exit wound with sterile dressings. Lay the casualty down in a half sitting position. Apply an elevation sling to the limb on the injured side. Tie a broad bandage across the sling.
For an elbow that can be bent: Call 995 for SCDF. Treat as for a fracture of the upper arm (see page 84).

For an elbow that cannot be bent: Call 995 for SCDF. DO NOT attempt to forcibly bend or straighten the elbow. Lay the casualty down and place the injured limb on the trunk. Bandage the injured limb to the trunk, first at the wrist and hips, then above the elbow.
Forearm and Wrist Fracture: Call 995 for SCDF. Treat as for a fracture of the upper arm (see page 84).

Actions to Take for Upper Arm Fracture: Sit the casualty down. Place the injured arm across his/her chest in a position that is most comfortable. Get him/her to support the arm if possible. Support the injured arm in a large arm sling. Tie a broad-fold bandage around the chest over the sling.
Actions to Take for Elbow Fracture: Call 995 for SCDF. Treat as for a fracture of the upper arm (see page 84).
Actions to Take for Forearm and Wrist Fracture: Call 995 for SCDF. Treat as for a fracture of the upper arm (see page 84).

title: Actions to Take
summary: Instructions for treating various types of fractures, including upper arm, elbow, forearm and wrist, and hand and fingers fractures.
subtopics: For an elbow that can be bent: Call 995 for SCDF. Treat as for a fracture of the upper arm (see page 84).

For an elbow that cannot be bent: Call 995 for SCDF. DO NOT attempt to forcibly bend or straighten the elbow. Lay the casualty down and place the injured limb on the trunk. Place soft padding between the injured limb and the body to ensure that bandaging will not displace the broken bones. Bandage the injured limb to the trunk, first at the wrist and hips, then above the elbow (see figure 87 on page 95).

Forearm and Wrist Fracture: Call 995 for SCDF. Expose and treat any open wounds. Gently place soft padding around the forearm. Support the arm in an arm sling (see figure 59 on page 68). Secure the arm to the chest with a broad-fold bandage tied over the sling, close to the elbow (see figure 86 on page 94). Tie the knot of the broad bandage in front on the uninjured side.

Hand and Fingers Fracture: Call 995 for SCDF. Protect the injured hand by placing soft padding around the hand. Gently support the injured arm in an elevation sling (see figure 60 on page 69). Secure the arm to the chest by applying a broad-fold bandage over the sling (see figure 85 on page 94). Tie the knot in front on the uninjured side.
evidence_keywords: Treat as for a fracture of the upper arm
DO NOT attempt to forcibly bend or straighten the elbow
Expose and treat any open wounds
Protect the injured hand by placing soft padding around the hand

title: Chemical Burn
summary: Chemical burns are caused by caustic or corrosive substances coming into contact with the skin. Treatment involves flushing the area with large amounts of water for 15 – 20 minutes or longer, and removing contaminated clothing.
subtopics: ✓ Flush the area immediately with large amounts of water for 15 – 20 minutes or longer.
✓ Wear gloves, apron and eye protection if available.
✓ Remove the casualty’s contaminated clothing whilst flushing.
✓ Cover the burned area with a dry clean dressing.
✓ Call 995 for SCDF. Inform the dispatch that chemicals are involved.

Sudden Cardiac Arrest may occur. Perform Chest Compressions and use the AED if casualty’s breathing stops.

title: Poisoning
summary: Describes the process and condition of poisoning, its types (acute and chronic), and the signs and symptoms that may occur depending on the substance, dose, and exposure.

title: Actions to Take
summary: Instructions for handling poisoning cases, including performing the Primary Survey, minimizing casualty movements, and ensuring personal safety.
subtopics: Do not force casualty to vomit or drink water

title: Transportation of Casualty
summary: This page provides guidance on the transportation of a casualty, including important factors to consider, methods for moving the casualty, and principles of lifting.
subtopics: Important factors when considering before moving the casualty

title: Moving a Casualty
summary: This page provides information on how to move a casualty safely and effectively.

title: Moving a Casualty
summary: This page provides information on methods for moving a casualty, including cradle carry, fireman's carry, pick-a-back carry, and two rescuer methods.

title: Pick-a-Back Carry
summary: When injuries make the fireman's carry unsafe, this method is used to transport a casualty.
subtopics: Crouch in front of the conscious casualty, with your back to him
Ask the casualty to put his arms over your shoulders and clasp his hands in front of you
Grasp the casualty's thighs and rise slowly, keeping your back straight

title: Two Rescuers Methods
summary: This page describes two methods for two rescuers to carry a casualty: Two-Handed Seat Carry and Four-Handed Seat Carry.

title: Improvised Methods
summary: Methods for transporting a casualty when no equipment is available
